stem_text: Potential energy ( 𝑉 ) versus distance ( 𝑥 ) is given by the graph. Rank various regions as per the magnitudes of the force ( 𝐹 ) acting on a particle from high to low. [FIG-stem-1]
interpretation: Rank force magnitudes |F| = |-dV/dx| from highest to lowest across regions AB, BC, CD, DE based on graph slopes.

candidate_solve.assumed_parameters_from_coaching_figure: V(x) piece-wise linear segments: AB from (0,0) to (1,1); BC from (1,1) to (2,4); CD from (2,4) to (4,4); DE from (4,4) to (6,3).
candidate_solve.derivation: Conservative force magnitude is given by |F| = |-dV/dx| = |slope|. Slope_AB = (1-0)/(1-0) = 1 => |F_AB| = 1. Slope_BC = (4-1)/(2-1) = 3 => |F_BC| = 3. Slope_CD = (4-4)/(4-2) = 0 => |F_CD| = 0. Slope_DE = (3-4)/(6-4) = -0.5 => |F_DE| = 0.5. Descending rank: |F_BC| (3) > |F_AB| (1) > |F_DE| (0.5) > |F_CD| (0).
candidate_solve.limiting_cases: Flat region CD has zero slope, hence minimum force (0). Steeper segment BC has maximum slope (3). Rank order is strictly determined by geometric steepness.

sl2.crux: Translating graph slopes of potential energy V(x) to conservative force magnitudes |F| = |dV/dx| and ordering piecewise segments.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Connection between conservative force and potential gradient.

representation_translation.evidence: Extracting coordinates and calculating slopes from piecewise graph.

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Calculate four segment slopes and order descendingly.

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Magnitude requested, so negative slope in DE becomes positive 0.5, exceeding flat CD.

wrong_route_hypotheses.route: Confusing force magnitude with potential energy value (ranking by V instead of slope)
Retaining negative sign for DE slope (-0.5 < 0) placing DE below CD
